> 天下有至樂無有哉？有可以活身者無有哉？

Is there such a thing as supreme joy? Is there a way to keep a body alive? Then: what to do, what to lean on, what to avoid, where to stay, what to approach, what to leave, what to love, what to hate.

Eight questions in one breath, and the chapter answers the first one with three characters: 至樂無樂.

## 至樂無樂 is not "no joy"

至: at the limit. 至樂無樂: joy at its limit is not joy — meaning, it no longer measures itself with the pair joy／suffering.

This is the difference between "I feel nothing" and "I am no longer using that ruler." The first is numbness. The second is the ruler being put down.

## 惛惛: what long life costs

惛惛: dim, muddled. The long-lived are described as 惛惛 — still alive, the spirit already blurred.

One word, and the account of longevity is settled. The chapter is not against living long. It is against the bill, which is usually not shown.

## 誙誙然: the shape of a crowd running

誙誙然如將不得已 — running in a pack as though unable to do otherwise.

Six characters for every crowd you have ever been in: no one knows why, and everyone is moving. Note the word 不得已 again — the same two characters that in 人間世 mean "the moment arrived." Here they are being misused, and the misuse is exactly what the chapter is pointing at.

## 蹲循

蹲循 reads 逡巡: to withdraw, to circle without advancing. 忠諫不聽，蹲循勿爭 — if honest counsel is not heard, withdraw and do not fight over it.

## 褚小綆短

褚: a sack. 綆: the rope on a well bucket.

褚小者不可以懷大，綆短者不可以汲深 — a small sack cannot hold something large; a short rope cannot reach deep water.

This is the chapter's most concrete instrument. It is not a metaphor about ambition. It is a statement about capacity and reach, and it cuts in both directions: the tool that is too small fails, and the tool that is too large is also a mismatch.

## 髑髏 and the four characters of its refusal

The skull is asked whether it wants to be restored to life, to family, to speech. Its answer is delivered 矉蹙頞 — brow knit, nose bridge drawn up: refusal, in four characters, before any word arrives.

The passage is usually read as a meditation on death. Read it as a passage about being asked: the skull is being offered a return, and the offer is a proposal made by someone who cannot see the position of the one being offered.

## 幾: the germ of change

幾 (in some editions 機): the minute, the incipient, the first movement of 造化 in a thing.

The last section lands here — on the almost-nothing that is before anything happens. Not a plan, not a principle. The instant at which something is about to become.

## 條達而福持

條達: unobstructed, flowing. 福持: the steady holding of what is good.

The chapter's closing definition of well-being: 名止於實，義設於適 — the name stops at the fact, the rightness is set to what fits. Then this steadiness follows on its own, without being sought.

## The test

Name the ruler you use to check whether you are doing well — a score, a comparison, a picture of a good life. Then ask: is this joy, or is this the ruler? 至樂無樂 is not an instruction to stop feeling. It is an instruction to notice which instrument is in your hand.
